senses.gloss: to stir up, to set in commotion.
units: <cite ref="Sifrei Devarim 39">Sifré Deut. 39</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 859:2">Yalk. ib. 859</cite> <he>יכול יהו מים גּוֹרְשִׁין את העפר ממקום בקעה וכ׳</he> you might suppose the (rain) water will stir up the (fat) ground of the valley, and thus the valley will lack (drinking) water.

senses.gloss: (cmp. טָרַד) to banish; to send off, divorce (a wife).—Part. pass. גָּרוּשׁ, f. גְּרוּשָׁה q. v.

units: Gen. R. s. 21.—Esp. to give a letter of divorce.
<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 9:1">Gitt. IX, 1</cite> <he>הַמְּגָרֵשׁ וכ׳</he> if one divorces his wife and says, on handing her the letter, &c.; a. v. fr.—
Ib. VI, 5 if one says (to his delegates) … גָּרְשׁוּהָ ga’rshuha, they are authorized to write and deliver to her a letter of divorce (geresh being the colloquial term for divorcing).
Pirké d’R. El. ch. XIX; XX ג׳ ויצא וכ׳ he was banished and he left paradise.—Part. מְגוּרָשׁ, f. מְגוּרֶשֶׁת.

<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 7:4">Gitt. VII, 4</cite> <he>מג׳ ואינה מג׳</he> she is and is not divorced, i.e. her divorce is doubtful, and she has to suffer the disqualifications of a married and of a divorced woman.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 92:4">Midr. Till. to Ps. XCII</cite>.

<cite ref="Gittin 65a:7">Gitt. 65ᵃ</cite> <he>מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת בקידושי וכ׳</he> she is entitled to receive a letter of divorce for herself even though her father had contracted the marriage in her behalf; a. v. fr. [

senses.gloss: to be stirred up, become muddy, thick. Midr. d’R. Akiba, Alef (Jellinek Beth Hammidrash III, 13).]
